name: OpenKilda
what_it_is: OpenKilda is a web-scale Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controller built by Telstra, capable of managing tens of thousands of OpenFlow switches simultaneously and controlling millions of flows. It is based on Floodlight and uses Kafka and Apache Storm for distributed processing.
components: Floodlight Controllers (Floodlight 1 and 2) — OpenFlow switch controllers
Apache Storm Topology — distributed workflow and flow-rule computation
Apache Kafka — message bus between components
OrientDB — graph database for topology and flow state
Path Computation Engine — calculates routes using configurable cost functions
confd — template-based configuration management (YAML + Go templates)
GUI — web-based network monitoring and management
Telemetry and Reporting — sub-second network metrics visualization
measurement: Visualized network monitoring via built-in reporting component
Mirroring and data gathering for traffic analysis
configuration: confd with YAML variable files and Go-template formatting for all service configuration
Multi-table pipeline mode (default; single-table mode deprecated since release 1.126.2)
Blue-green deployment configuration for zero-downtime upgrades
Path cost functions are configurable in the Path Computation Engine
Flow groups configurable for backup route diversity
fault_injection: Virtual topology creation for test mode (simulated switch/link failures)
Flow groups with backup routes to validate failover behaviour
Path recalculation triggered on hardware change events
modes: Blue-green mode — two simultaneous controller versions for zero-downtime deployment
Debug mode — JDWP remote debugging enabled
Test mode — virtual topology creation for automated testing
constraints: Linux kernel 4.18+ required for Open vSwitch (OVS) meters support
Single-table switch mode is deprecated since release 1.126.2; new features are multi-table mode only
Build requires Gradle 7.0+, Maven 3.3.9+, JDK 8+, Python 3.8+, Docker 19.03.3+, GNU Make 4.1+
Supports up to tens of thousands of switches — not validated beyond that scale boundary
docker_services: docker-compose.yml not found at master or main branch roots; service count of ~10 sourced from entry metadata only — individual service names could not be verified from raw file fetch
notable_absences: No documented fault injection tooling beyond virtual topology and path recalculation
No documented performance benchmarks or latency thresholds
docker-compose.yml not accessible via raw GitHub (404 on both master and main branches), so service details are unverified
